logline: A thousand-year-old hotel for restless ghosts is run by a beautiful, wrathful owner bound there by ancient punishment - until a reluctant Harvard-trained manager gets tangled in her world.

renewal.note: Single-season limited series; concluded September 1, 2019. A US-set remake is in development at Skydance Media. A stage musical adaptation premiered in South Korea in 2022.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb settled at 8.1 from a large base. Viewership peaked at 12.001 percent nationwide - exceptional for a cable run. IU's Baeksang Best Actress nomination confirmed industry respect for the lead performance. The back half is weaker than the front, which caps the score.

seasons.review_body: Hotel del Luna aired on tvN from July 13 to September 1, 2019, reaching peak nationwide cable viewership of 12.001 percent. IU portrays Man-wol, turning 1,300 years of sorrow into a weaponized contempt, and the performance sells the fantasy with sheer conviction. Yeo Jin-goo anchors the mortal-world logic as Chan-sung, the Harvard MBA pulled into her orbit. Production design and the original soundtrack stand out with strong acclaim. A US remake entered development at Skydance Media. The back half of the season loosens structural tightness as the episodic ghost-of-the-week format gives way to Man-wol's backstory reveals, shifting tone toward more melodrama even as the first eight episodes maintain a cleaner elegance. IMDb lists the series at 8.1, and the finale posts an 8.6 episode rating, marking an ending that lands for the core storyline arc after the mid-season slowdown.

episode_reviews.title: Welcome to Hotel del Luna
episode_reviews.review_body: Hotel del Luna premiered July 13, 2019 on tvN and established the show's visual and tonal register with precision that made its peak nationwide cable viewership of 12.001 percent feel earned over sixteen episodes. The premise - a thousand-year-old hotel for unresolved ghosts, run by a proprietor bound there by ancient punishment - is introduced through the design of the hotel itself: a crumbling palace hidden in plain sight within modern Seoul, rendered with production values that set an immediate standard. IU's Man-wol entrance in the hotel lobby - costume, lighting, and her stillness doing more worldbuilding than the surrounding dialogue - is the premiere's defining image and the moment the show signals that its fantasy register is committed rather than decorative. The IMDb 8.1 series score and IU's subsequent Baeksang Best Actress nomination reflect a performance the premiere plants fully from the first scene.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the hotel's rules, with ghosts tied to unresolved business, a proprietor who hates being disturbed, and the reluctant manager's induction into this world. The visual design lands as immediately distinct: a crumbling palace hidden in plain sight within modern Seoul.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Man-wol's first full entrance in the hotel lobby - costume, lighting, and IU's stillness doing more worldbuilding than the dialogue.

episode_reviews.title: Lunar Eclipse
episode_reviews.review_body: Hotel del Luna Episode 13 'Lunar Eclipse' aired August 25, 2019 on tvN and was tracked by audience reviewers as the season's highest-scoring episode outside the finale block, with an IMDb episode rating of 8.5. The episode shifts the show's weight from episodic ghost resolution to Man-wol's ancient debt - the mythology the series had been building toward across twelve episodes of ghost-of-the-week structure. Hong Jung-eun and Hong Mi-ran's writing in this episode demonstrates the show at its most tonally balanced: the wry register of the early episodes maintained while the emotional stakes of Man-wol's backstory reach their most direct expression. The lunar eclipse sequence - where the show's visual ambition and emotional stakes align in a single sustained image - is the episode's most frequently cited moment among the series' international audience.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: An episode that audience trackers rated 8.5 on IMDb - the season's highest-scoring episode outside the finale block. The emotional weight shifts here from episodic ghost resolution to Man-wol's ancient debt, and the show demonstrates that it can sustain its mythology without losing the wry tone that made the early episodes work.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The lunar eclipse sequence - a rare moment where the show's visual ambition and its emotional stakes align perfectly.
